title: Feasibility study on the implementation of the new prostate cancer screening recommendation in Germany: PSA measurement using capillary blood sampling (PRO-KAP)
summary:
Prostate cancer is the most common type of cancer among men in Germany. Early detection improves the chances of recovery.
Since 2025, medical guidelines have recommended a blood test to measure the prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level instead of the digital rectal examination previously offered. This marker can indicate the risk of developing prostate cancer. Experts have managed to simplify the necessary blood test: It was shown that only a few drops of blood are needed from a small prick in the fingertip or earlobe (as is done, for example, to measure blood sugar in diabetes). This can be done at the National Cancer Prevention Center in Heidelberg.
Participants are also asked to complete a short anonymous online questionnaire to identify reasons and possible barriers to participating in early detection.
The project is part of the European Joint Action "EUCanScreen".

interventions.name: Men aged 49-51 years from the study region Heidelberg are invited for a PSA measurement using capillary blood at the prevention outpatient clinic of the National Cancer Prevention Center (NCPC).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
living in the study region Heidelberg; receipt of invitation letter
Exclusion criteria:
previous diagnosis of prostate cancer; biopsy of the prostate within 6 months prior to the invititation
